Surat "al-Qadr" is Medinan according to the view of most exegetes, as mentioned by al-Tha'labi. Al-Mawardi reported the opposite. I say: it is Medinan according to al-Dahhak and one of the two opinions of Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Waqidi mentioned that it was the first surah to be revealed in Medina. It has five verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Indeed, We revealed it during the Night of Decree.﴾ (97:1)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We revealed it﴾ means the Qur'an, even though it has not been mentioned in this surah, because the meaning is known, and the entire Qur'an is like a single surah. He has said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and He said: ﴿Ha-Mim. By the Clear Book. Indeed, We revealed it during a blessed night﴾ [al-Dukhan: 1-3], meaning: during the Night of Decree. Al-Sha'bi said: the meaning is that We began its revelation during the Night of Decree. It was also said: rather, Jibril, peace be upon him, brought it down as a whole in one piece during the Night of Decree, from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, to the House of Honour (Bayt al-'Izzah), and Jibril dictated it to the scribes (al-safarah) [[al-safarah: they are the angels, plural of safir. The safir originally means the scribe, so called because he clarifies and makes clear the matter.]], then Jibril would reveal it to the Prophet ﷺ in installments [[i.e., part by part, a verse or two at a time.]]. Between its beginning and its end was twenty-three years, so said Ibn 'Abbas, and this has been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah [[See vol. 2, p. 297, second edition.]]. Al-Mawardi related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The Qur'an was revealed in the month of Ramadan, in the Night of Decree, in a blessed night, as a whole from Allah, from the Preserved Tablet to the noble scribes (al-safarah al-kiram al-katibin) in the lowest heaven, and then the noble scribes revealed it to Jibril in installments over twenty years, and Jibril revealed it to the Prophet ﷺ in installments over twenty years. Ibn al-'Arabi said: This is false; there is no intermediary between Jibril and Allah, nor between Jibril and Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿during the Night of Decree﴾. Mujahid said: during the Night of Judgment.

(﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾) He said: it is the Night of Judgment. The meaning is the Night of Measuring (al-taqdir), so named because Allah, may He be exalted, determines in it what He wills of His affair until the same night of the following year, concerning death, lifespan, provision, and other matters [[He means that He manifests what He decreed in eternity, not that He determines it anew.]]. And He hands it over to the executors of affairs, who are four of the angels: Israfil, Mika'il, 'Izra'il, and Jibril, peace be upon them. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: What will occur in the year of provision, rain, life, and death is written from the Mother of the Book, even the pilgrims. 'Ikrimah said: The pilgrims to the House of Allah, may He be exalted, are written on the Night of Decree by their names and the names of their fathers; none of them is left out, and none is added to them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said this. This meaning has already passed at the beginning of Surat al-Dukhan [[See vol. 16, p. 125.]]. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah, may He be exalted, decides the decrees on the night of the middle of Sha'ban, and hands them over to their owners on the Night of Decree. It was also said: it is called that only because of its greatness, its worth, and its nobility, from the saying: "So-and-so has a qadr," meaning nobility and standing. This was said by al-Zuhri and others. It was also said: it is called that because acts of worship have great worth in it and abundant reward. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: it is called that because whoever has no worth or standing becomes one of worth on this night if he spends it in worship. It was also said: it is called that because Allah sent down in it a Book of worth, upon a Messenger of worth, to a community of worth. It was also said: because angels of worth and dignity descend in it. It was also said: because Allah, may He be exalted, sends down in it goodness, blessing, and forgiveness. Sahl said: it is called that because Allah, may He be exalted, decreed in it mercy for the believers. Al-Khalil said: because the earth becomes constricted in it by the angels, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whose provision is restricted﴾ [al-Talaq: 7], meaning: constricted.

The Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 97, verses 2–3:

Al-Farra' said: Every occurrence in the Qur'an of His words, "And what will make you know" (wa ma adraka), He did inform (the Prophet) of it. And whatever occurs in His words, "And what will make you know" (wa ma yudrika) [al-Ahzab: 63], He did not inform him of it. Sufyan also said this. This has been discussed earlier.[[See vol. 18, p. 257, vol. 19, p. 247, and p. 3 of this part.]]

"The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months" (laylatu al-qadr khayrun min alfi shahr). This shows its excellence and greatness. The excellence of a time comes only from the abundance of virtues that occur within it. On that night, abundant good is apportioned that is not found in a thousand months. And Allah knows best.

Many exegetes (mufassirun) said: that is, the work done in it is better than work done in a thousand months that do not contain the Night of Decree. Abu al-Aliyah said: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree. It was also said: By "a thousand months" He meant the entire age (al-dahr), because the Arabs use "a thousand" to mean the extreme limit of things, as He, the Exalted, said: "Each of them wishes he could be given a life of a thousand years" [al-Baqarah: 96],[[Verse 96 of Surah al-Baqarah.]] meaning the entire age.

It was also said: In the past, a worshipper was not called a worshipper until he had worshipped Allah for a thousand months, that is, eighty-three years and four months. So Allah, the Exalted, granted to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) the worship of one night, which is better than a thousand months of the worship they used to perform.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: The kingdom of Sulayman lasted five hundred months, and the kingdom of Dhu al-Qarnayn lasted five hundred months, so their kingdoms together came to a thousand months. Allah, the Exalted, made the work done on this night, for whoever attains it, better than their kingdom.

Ibn Mas'ud said: The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who wore weapons in the way of Allah for a thousand months. The Muslims were amazed at this, and then the verse "Indeed, We sent it down" [al-Qadr: 1] was revealed, "is better than a thousand months," the months in which that man wore his weapons in the way of Allah. Similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: That man was a Muslim, and his mother had dedicated him to Allah as a vow. He was from a village of people who worshipped idols, and he lived near them. He began to raid them alone, killing, taking captives, and striving. He would meet them only with a jawbone of a camel (bi-lihyay ba'ir).[[Al-lihan (with the lam vowelled and doubled, and the ha' sukun): the bone of the jaw on which the teeth sit. The wording of al-Tabari in his History (European edition, first part, p. 794) is: "When he met them, he met them with a camel's jawbone, and he met them with nothing else. When they fought him and he fought them, and he grew tired and thirsty, pure water gushed for him from the stone that was in the jawbone..." etc., with the word "al-lihy" in the singular in both places.]] When he fought them and they fought him, and he became thirsty, pure water gushed for him from the two jawbones, and he drank from it. He had been given great strength in seizing, and neither iron nor anything else could hurt him. His name was Shamshun.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: He was a king among the Children of Israel who did one good deed. Allah revealed to the prophet of their time: "Tell so-and-so to make a wish." The man said: "O Lord, I wish to strive with my wealth, my children, and myself." So Allah gave him a thousand children. He would equip a child with his wealth in an army and send him out to strive in the way of Allah. He would stand (in prayer) for a month, and that child would be killed. Then he would equip another in an army, and every child was killed within a month, while the king kept vigil at night and fasted by day. Thus a thousand children were killed in a thousand months. Then he advanced himself, fought, and was killed. The people said: "No one can attain the rank of this king." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months," that is, better than the months of that king in standing (in prayer), fasting, and striving with wealth, self, and children in the way of Allah.[[Note: In the source, the Arabic grammatical remark on counting refers to the forms "alf al-walad" and "al-alf al-walad": the Basrians said that when a number is in construct (idafah), the definite article is added only to its last element, while the Kufans permitted adding it to the first and the second. Thus, according to the Kufans, one would say here "alf al-walad" or "al-alf al-walad."]]

Ali and Urwah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned four men from the Children of Israel and said: "They worshipped Allah for eighty years and did not disobey Him for the blink of an eye." He named Ayyub, Zakariyya, Hizqil ibn al-'Ajuz, and Yusha' ibn Nun. The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) were amazed at this. Then Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, your community is amazed at the worship of these men for eighty years without disobeying Allah for the blink of an eye. Allah has sent down to you something better than that." Then he recited: "Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of Decree." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pleased by this.

Malik said in al-Muwatta', in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim and others: I heard from one whom I trust say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown the lifespans of the nations before him, and it seemed to him that the lifespans of his community were short, so that they would not reach in deeds what others reached through long life. So Allah, the Exalted, gave him the Night of Decree and made it better than a thousand months.

In al-Tirmidhi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown the Banu Umayyah on his pulpit, and that grieved him. So the verse was revealed: "Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar" [al-Kawthar: 1], meaning a river in Paradise. And the verse was revealed: "Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of Decree. And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months," which the Banu Umayyah will rule after you. Al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Hudani said: We counted it, and it came to exactly a thousand months, neither more by a day nor less by a day. He said: It is a strange (gharib) hadith.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 97, verse 4:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿The angels descend﴾, meaning they come down from every heaven, and from Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary), and the dwelling place of Jibril (Gabriel), upon him be peace, is in its midst. So they descend to the earth and say "Amin" to the supplications of the people, until the time of the rising of dawn. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "The angels descend."

(And the Spirit therein, by the permission of their Lord) meaning Jibril, upon him be peace. Al-Qushayri related that the Spirit is a category of the angels, who were made guardians over the rest of them, and that the angels do not see them, just as we do not see the angels. Muqatil said: they are the most noble of the angels and the closest of them to Allah, may He be exalted. It was also said: they are an army from among the armies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, other than the angels. This was narrated by Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and mentioned by al-Mawardi. Al-Qushayri related: it was said they are a kind of creation of Allah who eat food, have hands and feet, and are not angels. It was also said: the Spirit is a great creation who stands in a row, and all the angels stand in a row. It was also said: the Spirit is mercy, with which Jibril, upon him be peace, descends along with the angels on this night upon its people. Its evidence is His saying: "He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants" [[Verse 2 of Surah an-Nahl.]] [an-Nahl: 2], meaning with mercy. ﴿Therein﴾, meaning in the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). ﴿By the permission of their Lord﴾, meaning by His command.

(From every command): they are commanded with every matter that Allah has decreed and determined in that year until the next, as said by Ibn Abbas, like His saying: "They guard him by the command of Allah" [[Verse 11 of Surah ar-Ra'd.]] [ar-Ra'd: 11], meaning by the command of Allah. The common reading is "tanazzalu" with a fatha on the ta', except that al-Bazzi doubled the ta'. Talhah ibn Musarrif and Ibn as-Sumayqa read it with a damma on the ta' as a passive verb. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and al-Kalbi read "min kulli amr" (from every matter). It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that its meaning is: from every angel. Al-Kalbi interpreted it to mean that Jibril descends therein with the angels, and they greet every Muslim person.

(Min) here means "upon" (ʿala). It is related from Anas that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Night of Power comes, Jibril descends in a kabkabah (a closely packed group) [[Al-kabkabah (with a fatha): a crowd gathered closely together of people or others.]] of angels, who pray and greet every servant, standing or sitting, who remembers Allah, may He be exalted."

It is said: the complete sentence is "from every matter," then He said "Peace." This is narrated from Nafi' and others. That is, the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) is peace, and all of it is good, with no evil in it. ﴿Until the rising of dawn﴾, that is, until the emergence of dawn. Ad-Dahhak said: "Allah decrees nothing in that night except peace, whereas in all other nights He decrees afflictions and well-being." It is also said: that is, it is peace, meaning it is free from any devil being able to affect a believing man or woman. Mujahid likewise said: "It is a night of safety; Satan cannot do any evil or harm in it." This is also narrated as a marfu' (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ) report. Ash-Sha'bi said: "It is the greeting of the angels to the people of the mosques, from the time the sun sets until dawn rises. They pass by every believer and say: 'Peace be upon you, O believer.'" It is also said: it means the angels greeting one another in it. Qatadah said: "Salam hiya" means "it is good." ﴿Until the rising of dawn﴾, that is, until the rising (matla') of dawn.

Al-Kisa'i and Ibn Muhaysin read (matli'i) with a kasra on the lam; the rest read it with a fatha. Both fatha and kasra are two dialects (lughatan) for the verbal noun (masdar). The fatha is the original form of fa'ala–yaf'ulu (as in al-maqtal and al-makhraj), while the kasra is of what deviates from its regular pattern, as in al-mashriq, al-maghrib, al-manbit, al-maskan, al-mansik, al-mahshar, al-masqit and al-majzir. In all of these both fatha and kasra have been reported, when intended as a verbal noun rather than a noun of place.

Here there are three issues.

The first: on the determination of the Night of Power, the scholars have differed. The view held by most is that it is the twenty-seventh night, based on the hadith of Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Your brother Abdullah ibn Mas'ud says: whoever stands (in prayer) the whole year will find the Night of Power." He said: "May Allah forgive Abu Abd al-Rahman! He knew that it is in the last ten nights of Ramadan, and that it is the twenty-seventh night, but he wanted people not to rely on it alone." Then he swore, without making an exception [[i.e., he affirmed it firmly in his oath without adding the qualification "if Allah wills" after it.]], that it is the twenty-seventh night. I said: "How do you know that, O Abu al-Mundhir?" He said: "By the sign which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us about, or by the sign that the sun rises on that day without its rays." At-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan sahih hadith." Muslim also transmitted it.

It is also said that it is in Ramadan alone and not in the rest of the year; this was said by Abu Hurairah and others. It is also said that it is in all the nights of the year.

Therefore, whoever attaches the divorce of his wife or the manumission of his slave to the Night of Power, the emancipation and divorce do not take effect until a year has passed from the day of the oath, because it is not permissible to effect divorce on the basis of doubt, and it has not been established that it is specific to a particular time; so divorce should not take effect except after a full year has elapsed. The same applies to manumission and whatever is similar to it, such as oaths or other matters.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever stands (in prayer) the whole year will find it." This reached Ibn Umar, who said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu Abd al-Rahman! Indeed he knew that it is in the last ten nights of the month of Ramadan, but he wanted people not to rely on it alone." To this view Abu Hanifah went, that it is in the whole year. It was reported from him that it has been lifted (rufi'at), meaning the Night of Power, and that it occurred only once; but the correct view is that it remains.

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud: that if it falls on a certain day in one year, it will fall on a different day the following year. The majority hold that it occurs every year in Ramadan.

Then it was said: it is the first night of the month. This was said by Abu Razin al-'Uqayli. Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: it is the night of the seventeenth of Ramadan, the night whose morning saw the Battle of Badr. It seems they derived this from the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿And what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], and that was on the night of the seventeenth. It was also said that it is the night of the nineteenth.

The correct and well-known view is that it is in the last ten nights of Ramadan; this is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i, al-Awza'i, Abu Thawr and Ahmad.

Then some people said: it is the night of the twenty-first. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, inclined to this, on the basis of the hadith of water and clay, narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, which Malik transmitted [[The wording of the hadith as narrated by Malik in the Muwatta': "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe seclusion (i'tikaf) in the middle ten nights of Ramadan. One year he observed seclusion, and when it was the night of the twenty-first, which is the night on whose morning he would emerge from his seclusion, he said: 'Whoever observed seclusion with me, let him observe seclusion in the last ten nights. I have seen this night, then I forgot it. I saw myself prostrating on its morning in water and clay, so seek it in the last ten nights, and seek it in every odd night.' Abu Sa'id said: 'The sky rained that night, and the mosque was roofed with palm branches, so the mosque leaked. Abu Sa'id said: My eyes saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ leave, and on his forehead and nose were traces of water and clay from the morning of the twenty-first night.']] and others.

It was also said that it is the night of the twenty-third, based on what Ibn Umar narrated: a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw the Night of Power on the seventh of the last (remaining) nights." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I see that your dreams agree on the twenty-third. So whoever wishes to stand in prayer during the month, let him stand on the night of the twenty-third." Ma'mar said: "Ayyub used to perform ghusl (ritual bath) on the night of the twenty-third and apply perfume." In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ said: "I saw that I was prostrating on its morning in water and clay." Abdullah ibn Unays said: "I saw him on the morning of the twenty-third night in water and clay, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had told us."

It was also said: the night of the twenty-fifth, based on the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek it in the last ten nights: on the ninth remaining, on the seventh remaining, on the fifth remaining." Narrated by Muslim. Malik said: "By the ninth he means the night of the twenty-first, by the seventh the night of the twenty-third, and by the fifth the night of the twenty-fifth."

It was also said: the night of the twenty-seventh. Its evidence has already passed, and this is the view of Ali, Aisha, Mu'awiyah and Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with them. Ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever seeks the Night of Power, let him seek it on the night of the twenty-seventh." Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'The Night of Power is the night of the twenty-seventh.'"

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "Allah the Exalted divided the nights of this month, the month of Ramadan, among the words of this surah. When He reached the twenty-seventh, He pointed to it, saying: 'It is.' Furthermore, the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) is mentioned three times, and it consists of nine letters, so it comes to twenty-seven."

It was also said: it is the night of the twenty-ninth, based on what is reported, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The Night of Power is the twenty-ninth or the twenty-seventh, and the angels on that night are as many as the pebbles." It has also been said that it is among the even nights [[plural of "shaf'," meaning a number that is divisible by two.]].

Al-Hasan said: "For twenty years I watched the sun on the night of the twenty-fourth, and I saw it rise white, without rays," meaning because of the abundance of lights on that night.

It was also said that it is hidden throughout the entire year, so that a person strives to spend all the nights in worship. It was also said: He hid it throughout the whole month of Ramadan, so that they strive in deeds and worship during the nights of Ramadan, in hope of attaining it, just as He hid the Middle Prayer among the prayers, His Greatest Name among His beautiful names, the time of answered supplication among the hours of Friday and the hours of the night, His anger in sins, His pleasure in acts of obedience, the Hour (the Last Day) among the times, and the righteous servant among the servants, out of mercy from Him and wisdom.

The second issue: on its signs. Among them, the sun rises on its morning white without rays. Al-Hasan said: The Prophet ﷺ said about the Night of Power: "Among its signs: it is a gentle, bright night, neither hot nor cold; the sun rises on its morning without rays." 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: "I was on the sea on the night of the twenty-seventh, so I took some of its water and found it sweet and pure."

The third issue: on its virtues. Sufficient for you is the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾, and His saying ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾. In the two Sahihs: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Power with faith and seeking reward, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sins," narrated by Abu Hurairah. Ibn Abbas said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "When the Night of Power comes, the angels who dwell in the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary descend, among them Jibril, and with them are banners; one banner is planted over my grave, another over Bayt al-Maqdis, another over the Masjid al-Haram, and another over Mount Sinai. They leave no believing man or woman without greeting them, except the habitual drinker of wine, the eater of pork, and the one who smears himself with saffron." And in the hadith: "Indeed Satan does not come out on this night until its dawn appears, he cannot harm anyone with madness or any corruption, and the sorcery of a sorcerer does not take effect in it."

Ash-Sha'bi said: "Its night is like its day, and its day like its night." Al-Farra' said: "Allah decrees in the Night of Power only happiness and blessings, and in other nights He decrees afflictions and punishments." This has already been reported from Ad-Dahhak. Such a matter cannot be said by personal opinion (ra'y), so it is traced back to the Prophet ﷺ. And Allah knows best.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said in the Muwatta': [Whoever attends the night prayer ('isha') of the Night of Power has taken his share of it] [[The words between the square brackets are an addition from the Muwatta'.]] [Such a matter is not reached by opinion.] Ubayd Allah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever prays the maghrib and the late 'isha' prayers in congregation on the Night of Power has taken his share of the Night of Power." Al-Tha'labi mentioned it in his tafsir [[In the copy of al-Tha'labi's tafsir available to us: "Whoever prays the maghrib and the late 'isha' on the Night of Power has taken ..." the hadith, and it does not mention "in congregation."]].

Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if I happen upon the Night of Power, what should I say?' He said: 'Say: O Allah, You are Forgiving and You love forgiveness, so forgive me.'"
